book_title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. VII, Part 2: Inscriptions of the Paramāras — Trivedi, Harihar Vithal (ed.)
quote: The expression Gurjarōchchhēda-nurbandhī applied to Vindhyavarman in verse 12 has a reference to his success in liberating the Paramāra kingdom which had suffered a disastrous plight at the hands of the Chaulukyas since the days of Yaśovarman whose kingdom had been captured by Jayasinha Siddharāja, as seen above.

book_title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. VII, Part 2: Inscriptions of the Paramāras — Trivedi, Harihar Vithal (ed.)
quote: This is so far the earliest known inscription connecting Dēvapāla, a scion of the Mahākumāra line with the main branch of the Paramāra family ruling at Dhāra. \( ^{4} \)  The latest known year of Arjunavarman of the main branch is 1215 A.C. when he issued the Sehōre grant: and when and how his rule ended is not known; but the statement of the present inscription shows that he was succeeded by Dēvapāla, some time before 1218 A.C. The difficulty that presents itself in the present inscription, however, is the mention of both the contradictory titles, viz., that of a feudatory and of an independent chief, associated with the name of Dēvapāla. This was already noted by Kielhorn while editing it, but he did not arrive at a satisfactory solution of the problem. And in view of both the contradictory titles attached to Dēvapāla's name in the present record, it appears very probable that in the first instance, in the natural course, he succeeded his father Harišchandra with the title of Mahākumāra, \( ^{6} \)  and for some time he may have ruled as a subordinate prince of the main branch; but soon after, with the end of the rule of Arjunavarman who may have left behind him no worthy person in the main branch, the throne of Dhāriā was also held by Devapāla, who styled himself as Paramabhattāraka, Mahāraṣiādhnaṇa and Paramēśvara.

book_title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. VII, Part 2: Inscriptions of the Paramāras — Trivedi, Harihar Vithal (ed.)
quote: The inscription does not specify Dêvapâla's relationship with Arjunavarman whom he is said to have succeeded, or the state of affairs leading to the former's accession. In this respect we have already seen in the preceding record that Arjunavarman of the main branch probably died without leaving a male heir, and Dêvapâla of the subordinate branch, who first succeeded his father Hariśchandra on the subordinate throne, seems to have had an opportunity of uniting both the houses and occupying the throne of Dhârâ.

book_title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. VII, Part 2: Inscriptions of the Paramāras — Trivedi, Harihar Vithal (ed.)

quote: The inscription refers itself to the auspicious and victorious reign of the illustrious Dēvapālādeva, who is evidently identical with the homonymous Paramāra ruler of Dhārā, whose earliest known date is furnished by the Harsūd or Harsaudā inscription to be V. 1275 and another by the Māndhātā grant dated in V. 1282.

book_title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. VII, Part 2: Inscriptions of the Paramāras — Trivedi, Harihar Vithal (ed.)
quote: This person was a son of Dēvapāla and the younger brother of Jaitugidēva, as we already know. And in view of the fact that Jaitugi's only date is recorded to be V. 1300 or 1243 A.C. \( ^{1} \) , the present inscription, which is the earliest of Jayasimha's reign, clearly indicates that he succeeded his elder brother Jaitugidēva sometime between 1243 and 1256 A.C. We also know that in Jaitugi's time Mālwā had suffered from the invasions of the Yādava Krishna from the south, of the Vāghēlas from the west, and also from the Muslim general Balban from the north: \( ^{5} \)  and the present inscription goes to indicate that in spite of all these odds, Jayavarman, besides maintaining the integrity of his kingdom, had successfully penetrated so far in the Saugor (Sāgar) District, following the foot-steps of his father, whose records are found in the Khanḍwā District which is to its west.

quote:
The plates were issued by the Mahārdjādhivāja, the illustrious Jayavarmadeva, the younger brother of Jaitugideva. They record the perpetual grant of the village Vadaūda, situated in the Mahuada-pathaka, to three Brāhmanas, hailing from different localities. The (produce of the) village was divided into six shares (vaittakus), so that one of the donees obtained four shares, and the other two, one share each.
In its initial portion the charter cites the same verses (1-22) as found in Devapala's Mändhātā grant, containing the genealogy of the house from Bhōja to Dēvapāla; \( ^{1} \) and new information is added thereafter in two stanzas (vv. 22-23), the first of which states that Dēvapāla was succeeded on the throne of Mālava by his son Jaitugi, who bore the epithet of Bālānārāyaṇa: \( ^{2} \) The second of these stanzas means to say that Jaitugi was succeeded by his younger brother Jayavarman, This account is followed by recording the purpose.

quote: \( ^{1} \)  Verse 52 is again historically important; it states, in a poetic way, that Jayasiniha was both — a dauhitra (daughter's son) as well as a pautra (son's son), so far as the succession in the Paramāra kingdom was concerned. From the latter of these statements, it would appear that Jayavarman's father Dēvapāla, under whom both the branches of the royal Paramāra house are known to have united, succeeded Arjunavarman as his son-in-law; this is a view which, if accepted, would dismiss the whole controversy regarding Dēvapāla's accession to the throne of Dihārā, viz., whether he captured Dihārā by overthrowing Arjunavarman, or, was a natural successor of him, when he died without leaving a male heir.

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: He was not only a great general but also a great poet and patron of art and literature. The poets Dhanika, Padmagupta, Amitagati and many others benefited from his munificence. He also dug many tanks and built a number of temples.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: With the accession of Bhōja (c.A.D.1000-c.A.D.1055), the son and successor of Sindhurāja, a brilliant chapter was opened in the history of the art and architecture of Mālava. Epigraphical evidence eloquently testifies his participation in a vigorous temple building activity.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: Second inscription mentions the name of the Paramāra king Udayāditya, beginning with Udayāditya-dēvasya. The third one consists of some Sanskrit grammatical rules.

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: \( ^{11} \)  The Paramāra princes moved to the east and established themselves in the region of Bhopal and Hoshangabad. Un, which lies in the west of the Mālava kingdom was, in all probability, lost its former glory and royal patronage in this period of political instability. We hear about several Paramāra princes who ruled in the eastern region of Mālava. They are as follows- Mahākumara Laksminīvarman, Mahākumāra Hariscandra, Mahākumara Trailokyavarman and Mahākumāra Udayavarman.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: The misfortune of the Paramāras continued to grow before it assumed serious proportion when Naravarmana (c.A.D.1093-1134) came to power. Harassed on all sides by the Cândellas, Cahamānas and Caulukyas, the Paramāra kingdom under Naravarmana steadily advanced towards its downfall. Though an incapable military leader, he was a talented poet and patron of learning. The Madhukargarh inscription records the construction of a Śiva temple by Haradeva, who took pride in having increased the glory of Naravarman.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: Taking advantage of the chaos and confusion created by the weakness of the later Paramāras, Ballāla an impostor of unknown identity usurped the power and began to rule Mālava from his capital at Dhārā. He was, however, not destined to rule for a long time. Kumārapāla (A.D. 1143-1173) the Caulukya king of Gujarat, sent an invading army against him. Ballāla was killed in a battle and, Mālava was brought under the Caulukya rule.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: After Subhaṭavarman's death, his son and successor Arjunavarman (c.A.D. 1210-1215) continued the traditional war with the Caulukyas of Gujarat. He defeated the Caulukya king Jayasīrīha, overran his kingdom and annexed Lāta to his kingdom. But he could not become successful against the Yādava ruler Simhāna (c.A.D.1210-1247). The Mamdapur inscription of 1251 A.D. shows that Simhāna decisively defeated and killed Arjunavarman.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Some Paramāra Temples From Madhya Pradesh: A Case Study of Village Un — Swati Mondal Adhikari
quote: A pillar inscription of Bhopal informs that the Lakṣmīvarman's feudatory Vijayasimha won a battle against his enemy. According to Trivedi, perhaps this enemy was the Cāndelāla king Madanavarman, with whom he had to fight in Mahādvādaśaka-manḍala (comprising parts of modern districts of Vidisha and Bhopal).
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship (Paramāra temples)

book_title: Madhya Pradesh District Gazetteers: Vidisha — Government of Madhya Pradesh
quote: The Chandelias were ousted from Malwa by the Paramara king Siyaka II, whose known date is A. D. 972. He founded an independent kingdom bounded by the Tapti on the south, modern Jhalawar on the north, Vidisha on the east and Sabarmati on the west. His son Munja Vakpatiraja II extended his father's territory further and further till he was defeated and killed by Taila II of the Chalukya house, in A. D.

book_title: Madhya Pradesh District Gazetteers: Vidisha — Government of Madhya Pradesh
quote: Son and successor of Sindhuraja was Bhoja Deva, the illustrious king of Malwa. He came to the throne about 1000 A. D. and ruled for more than half a century. Inscriptions of his reign, however, bear dates from A. D. 1020 to 1047. His kingdom included an area now represen.ed by Chittōr, Banswara, Dungarpur, Vidisha, Khandesh, Konkan, and upper course of the Godavari \( ^{1} \) At the end of Bhoja's life when his kingdom was attacked simultaneously by the Chaulukya king Bhima and Kalachuri monarch Gangeyadeva from west and east both, Vidisha might have been overrun by the Chedi force.
tier_note: T7 modern survey / Gazetteer: district Gazetteer, 1979 compilation: the modern setting

book_title: Madhya Pradesh District Gazetteers: Vidisha — Government of Madhya Pradesh
quote: What happened to this region during the fight of the next Paramara king Naravarman (A.D. 1094) with the Chaulukya ruler Jayasimha Siddharaja is not known. The next king Yasovarman was defeated by him and the whole of Malwa was annexed to his kingdom about A.D. 1135.

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote:
This made possible for the Rajput feudatory powers to assert their independence and as a result the new Rajput Houses of the Paramaras and the Kacchavahas first came into prominence dividing the territories of Madhya Bharat into the two sizeable kingdoms of Malwa and Gwalior respectively.
The Rajput house of Paramaras were formerly feudatories of the Rashtrakutas in Gujarat. When Rashtrakuta glory was waning away and the hold of Pratihara empire at Kanauj was slackening, Paramaras shifted themselves from Gujarat to Malwa. Siyaka II was perhaps the first independent Paramara ruler.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: Munja was succeeded by Bhoja (1010-1050 A. D.) the greatest monarch of the Paramara dynasty, famous in Indian legend and history. His claim to greatness rests more on his patronage of art and literature than on his political and military achievements.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: Bhoja rebuilt the old town of Dhara which had already become the capital of the Paramaras and raised it to the status of the great cities of his age. Of the few remnants of that glorious city, which are now left, the most notable is what is now the Kamal Maula's mosque said to have been once the great college known as Bhoja Shala called after the name of the founder.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: The earlier histored of the town is not definitely known but the numerous wooded groves and lakes nearabout it seem to have impressed upon the art-loving Paramara King Bhoja, who, eventually shifted his capital from Ujjain to Dhar and exerted personally in improving upon its natural surroundings.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: The number of the surviving examples of this full blown conception of architecture in Madhya Bharat is simply staggering. It seems a wave of temple building had then swept over this land; for, nine tenths of the ancient temples now existing belong to this age. Only few of them, the best ones can here be named such as those at Udaypur, Gwalior fort, Nemawar, Badoh, Gyaraspur, Un, etc.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: On the northern fringe of the Satpura ranges in the plain of Nimar lies a township named Un which it appears was a flourishing place some 1000 years ago; for about a dozen temples lie clustering about it representing an architecture patronised by the Paramara kings of Malwa.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: But by the middle of the twelfth century, a large portion of the Paramara territory, including Ujjuin, was lost to Siddharaja Jay Singh of Gujarat. Arjunavarman (1211-1215 A. D.) was the last able prince of the dynasty for his successor was called upon to bear the brunt of the Muslim invasions which finally brought down the Paramara rule once for all.
tier_note: T5 modern scholarship: modern scholarship and archaeological observation (Patil)

book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
quote: The Paramaras ruled over parts of Nimar including Maheshwar but they do not seem to have held the town in much importance.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज परमार राजवंश में उत्पत्र हुआ था । यह परमार राजवंश मालवा में शासन करता था । सीयक ढितीय (दसवीं शती) तक परमार राष्ट्रकृते के प्रतिनिधि के रूप में शासन करता था । इसका पुत्र वाक्पति मुंज (974-997 ई.) मालवा का स्वतंत्र शासक हो गया । इसने अपने पड़ौसी क्षेत्रों पर अधिकार कर पर्याप्त राज्य विस्तार किया । मुंज का अनुज सिन्धुराज (997-999 ई.) था ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja was born in the Paramara dynasty ruling Malwa; until Siyaka II they ruled as Rashtrakuta representatives; his son Vakpati Munja (974-997 CE) became independent ruler of Malwa and expanded his realm; Munja's younger brother was Sindhuraja (997-999 CE).
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Bhoja was born in the Paramara dynasty ruling Malwa; until Siyaka II they ruled as Rashtrakuta representatives; his son Vakpati Munja (974-997 CE) became independent ruler of Malwa and expanded his realm; Munja's younger brother was Sindhuraja (997-999 CE).

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
इसने कुन्तल तैलप द्वितीय को पराजित किया । हूणों को पराजित कर उसने वागड़ (वॉसवाझ-डूंगरपुर) क्षेत्र पर विजय प्राप्त की । तदूनन्तर उसने कौशल या छत्तीसगढ़ पर अधिकार किया । फिर लाख, अपरांत आदि जीतता हुआ वह दक्षिण में चोल, मुरल (केरल) को जीतते हुए उसने नागराज शंखपाल की पुत्री शशिप्रभा से विवाह किया था ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* He defeated Kuntala Tailapa II, conquered Vagad after defeating the Hunas, took Kosala, then Lata and Aparanta, and in the south Chola and Murala (Kerala); he married Shashiprabha, daughter of Nagaraja Shankhapala.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: He defeated Kuntala Tailapa II, conquered Vagad after defeating the Hunas, took Kosala, then Lata and Aparanta, and in the south Chola and Murala (Kerala); he married Shashiprabha, daughter of Nagaraja Shankhapala.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
परन्तु ऐसा शासक जिसकी इतिहास में उपस्थिति के सवल प्रमाण हो, जिसके अपने रचे ग्रंथ हो, जिसकी रचना की प्रामाणिकता समकालीन और परवर्ती ग्रन्थकार भी वार-वार प्रकट करते हों, जो विविध झानधाराओं का प्रमाण वन गया हो, जो लोककथाओं तथा अनुश्रुतियों का भी नायक बन गया हो, जिसके मन्दिरों-मूर्तियों-भवनों के निर्माण के प्रमाण सुलभ हों, जिसके ताम्रपत्र और शिलालेख भी प्राप्त हो रहे हों, जिसे तत्कालीन वैदिक औरे जैन सभी समान आदर देते रहे हों - ऐसा अकेला कोई राजा दिखाई देता है, सबसे अधिक जगमगाता कोई शिखर दिखाई देता है तो वह है राजा भोज ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* But a ruler whose presence in history rests on strong evidence, who wrote his own works, about whom temple, image and building construction is attested, whose copper plates and inscriptions survive, and whom Vedic and Jain alike honoured - only Raja Bhoja appears as such.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: But a ruler whose presence in history rests on strong evidence, who wrote his own works, about whom temple, image and building construction is attested, whose copper plates and inscriptions survive, and whom Vedic and Jain alike honoured - only Raja Bhoja appears as such.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज अपने कृतित्व, व्यक्तिव और व्यवहार तथा उदारता के कारण अपने पूरे राज्य में ही नहीं, पूरे भारत में लोकप्रिय रहा । भारत ही नहीं, भारत के वाहर विभिन्न देशों में भी राजा भोज का यश व्यापता रहा । मंगोलिया से वहाँ की मंगोली भाषा में प्राप्त पारंपरिक ग्रन्थ ‘आराजिवुजि’ (राजा भोज) इसका प्रबल प्रमाण है ।
राजा भोज धर्मविद्ध था, वह अपने युग के प्रचलित समस्त धर्मों-सम्पदायों की निजी महत्ता को पहचानता था। इसलिए सबके प्रति उसकी समान आस्था थी।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Raja Bhoja was popular across the kingdom and all India through his works, personality, conduct and generosity; his fame spread abroad, as a Mongolian traditional text on Raja Bhoja shows; he was a knower of dharma who recognised the worth of all prevailing sects and held equal faith in all.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Raja Bhoja was popular across the kingdom and all India through his works, personality, conduct and generosity; his fame spread abroad, as a Mongolian traditional text on Raja Bhoja shows; he was a knower of dharma who recognised the worth of all prevailing sects and held equal faith in all.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
यही नहीं तुरुक्कों (तुकों) से युध्ध करने पर भी उसने रचनाधर्म में भेदभाव नहीं माना। यही कारण है कि भोज और किसी तुरुक्क (तुकों) कवि की सम्मिलित रचना के प्रमाण कतिपय श्लोक भी पाये जाते हैं।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Even in fighting the Turks he made no distinction in creative work; verses jointly composed by Bhoja and a Turk poet are found.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Even in fighting the Turks he made no distinction in creative work; verses jointly composed by Bhoja and a Turk poet are found.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज ने परम्परानुसार 55 वर्ष 7 मास 3 दिन तक गोड़ देश और दक्षिणापथ सहित विस्तृत क्षेत्र पर राज्य किया था -
पंचाशत्वंचवर्पाणि सप्तमासदिनत्रयम् ।
भोजराजेन भोक्यः सगौड़ो दक्षिणापथः ।।
इससे प्रतीत होता है कि उसने अपने विस्तृत राज्यक्षेत्र पर दीर्घकाल तक शासन किया था ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* By tradition Bhoja ruled 55 years 7 months 3 days over a wide region including Gauda country and Dakshinapatha, which suggests a long rule.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: By tradition Bhoja ruled 55 years 7 months 3 days over a wide region including Gauda country and Dakshinapatha, which suggests a long rule.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज (999-1055 ई.) इसी सिन्धुराज का पुत्र था। उसके 1010 से 1055 ई. तक के कई ताप्रपत्र, शिलालेख या भूतिलेख प्राप्त होते हैं। एक ताप्रपत्र के अन्त में लिखा गया है - स्वहस्तोयं श्रीभुजदेवस्य । अर्थात् यह (ताप्रपत्र) भोजदेव ने अपने हाथ से लिखा (और दिया) है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Raja Bhoja (999-1055 CE) was this Sindhuraja's son; several copper plates, stone inscriptions and image inscriptions of 1010 to 1055 CE are found; one copper plate ends 'this is the own hand of Shri Bhojadeva', i.e. Bhojadeva wrote and gave it himself.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Raja Bhoja (999-1055 CE) was this Sindhuraja's son; several copper plates, stone inscriptions and image inscriptions of 1010 to 1055 CE are found; one copper plate ends 'this is the own hand of Shri Bhojadeva', i.e. Bhojadeva wrote and gave it himself.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
ताम्रपत्रों में भोज के प्रथमों की पुष्पिकाओं में उन्हें 'महाराजाधिराज परमेश्वर श्रीभोजदेव' कहा गया है। स्पष्ट ही राजा भोजीराजाओं के भी राजा थे।
*Gloss [my translation]:* In the colophons of the copper plates Bhoja is called 'Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara Shri Bhojadeva' - clearly a king of kings.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: In the colophons of the copper plates Bhoja is called 'Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara Shri Bhojadeva' - clearly a king of kings.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
ऐसे वारह मण्डलों के स्वामी राजा भोज के अधीन थे तव समरांगणसूत्रधार रचा गया। ऐसे मंडलों में अवन्ति मण्डल, पूर्णपथक मण्डल, मोहड़वासक, अर्थाएट मण्डल, स्थाली मण्डल, संगमखेट मण्डल, हूण मण्डल इत्यादि उल्लेखनीय हैं ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Lords of twelve such mandalas were subordinate to Bhoja when the Samarangana-sutradhara was composed; notable mandalas include Avanti, Purnapathaka, Mohadavasaka, Arthuna, Sthali, Sangamakheta and Huna.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Lords of twelve such mandalas were subordinate to Bhoja when the Samarangana-sutradhara was composed; notable mandalas include Avanti, Purnapathaka, Mohadavasaka, Arthuna, Sthali, Sangamakheta and Huna.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज परम दानी था । यह कहा जाता था कि श्रुओं को शुंखलावढ़ करने से लोहा और दानपत्र लिखने से भोज के राज्य में ताँव का अभाव होने लग गया था । यह अतिशयोक्ति हो सकती है परन्तु अमूलोक्ति नहीं हो सकती । स्वोक्ति इतिहास से भी यह सिद्ध है कि उसने अपने अनेक श्रुओं को पराजित किया था और अनेक तामप्रन जारी किये थे जिनमें से कुछ तो प्राप्त भी हो गये हैं ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja was supremely generous; it was said that fettering enemies exhausted iron and writing grant-plates exhausted copper in his kingdom; this may be exaggeration but not baseless, since history shows he defeated many enemies and issued many copper plates, some of which have been found.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Bhoja was supremely generous; it was said that fettering enemies exhausted iron and writing grant-plates exhausted copper in his kingdom; this may be exaggeration but not baseless, since history shows he defeated many enemies and issued many copper plates, some of which have been found.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज के सुदीर्घ शासनकाल में युद्ध के शंखनाद होते रहे, रणभेरी बजती रही। परन्तु वह शासन के सुनियोजन में दक्ष था। वह योजनावढ़ तरीकेसे शासन करता था। अधिकारीगण अपने-अपने विभाग दक्षता से सम्हालते थे। अतः राजा भोज अपने उन विश्वस्त सहयोगियों के भरोसे निश्चिन्त हो कलासाधना तथा साहित्यसाधना करता रहता था। कवियों, कलाकारों तथा विद्धानों का वह अद्धितीय आश्यदाता था। वह स्वयं गुणी था तथा गुणों का पारखी भी।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Though war-drums sounded through his long reign, he was skilled in administration; officials ran their departments competently, so he could pursue art and literature; he was an unequalled patron of poets, artists and scholars, himself accomplished and a connoisseur.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Though war-drums sounded through his long reign, he was skilled in administration; officials ran their departments competently, so he could pursue art and literature; he was an unequalled patron of poets, artists and scholars, himself accomplished and a connoisseur.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज न केवल मित्रों अपितु शत्रुओं के लिए भी अपने गुणों में आदर्श रहा । और वे भी भोज के समान स्वयं को घोंपित करवाने में गौरव का अनुभव करते थे । गुजरात के राजा कुमारपाल स्वयं को लघु भोजराज कहलाना पसन्द करते थे ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja was an ideal in virtues for friends and foes alike; they too felt pride in being likened to Bhoja; King Kumarapala of Gujarat liked to be called 'little Bhojaraja'.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Bhoja was an ideal in virtues for friends and foes alike; they too felt pride in being likened to Bhoja; King Kumarapala of Gujarat liked to be called 'little Bhojaraja'.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज महाराजाधिराज परमेश्वर तो था ही क्योंकि उसके प्रस्थों से भी झात होता है कि उसके अधीनस्थ वारह राजा थे । यह उपाधि उसके ताप्रपत्रों, शिलालेखों तथा प्रस्थों की पुष्पिकाओं में प्राप्त होती है । मालवमण्डन, मालवाधीश, मालवचकवर्ती, सर्वभौम, अविन्तनायक, धारेश्वर, त्रिभुवननारायण, रणरंगमल्ल, लोकनारायण, विदर्भराज, अहिराज या अहीन्द्र, अभिनवाजून, कृष्ण आदि कितने ही विफ्तवों से भोज मण्डित था ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja was Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara, for his works show twelve kings under him; the title appears in his copper plates, inscriptions and colophons; he bore epithets such as Malavamandana, Malavadhisha, Malavachakravartin, Sarvabhauma, Avantinayaka, Dhareshvara, Tribhuvananarayana, Ranarangamalla, Loknarayana, Vidarbharaja, Ahiraja, Abhinavarjuna, Krishna.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Bhoja was Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara, for his works show twelve kings under him; the title appears in his copper plates, inscriptions and colophons; he bore epithets such as Malavamandana, Malavadhisha, Malavachakravartin, Sarvabhauma, Avantinayaka, Dhareshvara, Tribhuvananarayana, Ranarangamalla, Loknarayana, Vidarbharaja, Ahiraja, Abhinavarjuna, Krishna.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज के ज्योतिर्यन्थ राजमूगांक का प्रकाशन ब्रह्मविद्या (4/3) में प्रक्राशित हुआ जो 964 शक (1042 ई.) में रचा गया।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja's astrological work Rajamriganka, published in Brahmavidya (4/3), was composed in Shaka 964 (1042 CE).
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Bhoja's astrological work Rajamriganka, published in Brahmavidya (4/3), was composed in Shaka 964 (1042 CE).

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
यह समस्त वारह राजसमूह जिस राजद्धडामणि की भुजास्तम्भ से वेंधी वृत्ति का है और जिसकी इच्छा से चारों ओर घूमता है। उस श्रीमान् पृथ्वी के एक मात्र राम (तुल्य मनोहर) रा(भो)जदेव ने शीघ्र ही अपनी वृष्टि से यन्त्र प्रपंचों सहित इस यन्त्राध्याय की रचना की 167
*Gloss [my translation]:* This whole circle of twelve kings, whose conduct is bound to the pillar of the arm of that crest-jewel of kings and moves around at his will - that glorious Bhojadeva, the one Rama of the earth, quickly composed this chapter on machines together with these elaborations of devices from his own intellect.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: This whole circle of twelve kings, whose conduct is bound to the pillar of the arm of that crest-jewel of kings and moves around at his will - that glorious Bhojadeva, the one Rama of the earth, quickly composed this chapter on machines together with these elaborations of devices from his own intellect.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज एक महान् निर्मति था। भोज ने सुरक्षा की दृष्टि से अपनी राजधानी उज्जेन से हटाकर धारा नगरी कर दी। भोज ने उसे नयं ति सरे से वसाया। वह नवनिर्मित नगरी लोकाकर्षक बन गयी थी।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Raja Bhoja was a great builder; for security he moved his capital from Ujjain to Dhara and settled it anew; the newly built city became attractive.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Raja Bhoja was a great builder; for security he moved his capital from Ujjain to Dhara and settled it anew; the newly built city became attractive.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज के समय से मालवा में निर्माण-कांति आ गयी थी। प्रासाद, मन्दिर, तालाव, प्रतिमार्ज़ बनती रहीं और पूरा मालवा इन अनोखी कलाकृतियों से भर गया। मन्दसीर जिला इस दृष्टि से अधिक समुद्ध है। वहाँ का हिंगलाजगढ़ तो तत्कालीन अप्रतिम प्रतिमाओं का अकृत खजाना है। आज मालवा में जो कुछ निर्मितियों के प्राचीन रूप दिखाई देते हैं, उनमें से बहुधा परमारकालीन हैं।
*Gloss [my translation]:* From Bhoja's time Malwa saw a revolution in construction: palaces, temples, tanks and images; Mandsaur district is rich, Hinglajgarh a treasury of images; most ancient structures seen in Malwa today are of the Paramara period.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: From Bhoja's time Malwa saw a revolution in construction: palaces, temples, tanks and images; Mandsaur district is rich, Hinglajgarh a treasury of images; most ancient structures seen in Malwa today are of the Paramara period.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
यह वताया जाता है कि धारा नगरी में चौरासी चौराहे थे और प्रत्येक पर एक-एक मंदिर था। भोज ने चित्तीड़ में मन्दिर वनवाया था और कश्मीर के कपटेश्वर में कृष्ण सहित मन्दिर वनवाया था।
*Gloss [my translation]:* It is said Dhara had eighty-four crossroads each with a temple; Bhoja built a temple at Chittor and one with Krishna at Kapateshvara in Kashmir.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: It is said Dhara had eighty-four crossroads each with a temple; Bhoja built a temple at Chittor and one with Krishna at Kapateshvara in Kashmir.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
प्रवन्धचित्नामणि के अनुसार भोज के 104 भवनों, ग्रन्थों और उपाधियों के एक ही नाम थे । इसकी पुष्टि जयवर्मदेव (1258 हैं.) के खण्डित लेख से भी होती है । इसके अनुसार राजा भोज ने 104 मेठ, त्रिकूट आदि प्रासाद वनवाये थे । इससे आगे का लेख खण्डित है । इससे पूर्वांतक प्रवन्धचिन्तामणि की वात की पुष्टि होती है । इन प्रासादों की चर्चा समरंगणसूत्रधार (अध्याय 55-56) में प्राप्त होती हैं ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* According to Prabandhachintamani Bhoja's 104 buildings, works and titles had the same name; this is confirmed by a fragmentary inscription of Jayavarmadeva (1258 CE) saying Raja Bhoja built 104 prasadas such as Meru and Trikuta; the rest is broken; it confirms Prabandhachintamani to that extent; these prasadas are discussed in Samarangana-sutradhara chapters 55-56.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: According to Prabandhachintamani Bhoja's 104 buildings, works and titles had the same name; this is confirmed by a fragmentary inscription of Jayavarmadeva (1258 CE) saying Raja Bhoja built 104 prasadas such as Meru and Trikuta; the rest is broken; it confirms Prabandhachintamani to that extent; these prasadas are discussed in Samarangana-sutradhara chapters 55-56.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
प्रभाच्चाचार्य के अनुसार धारा में 84 प्रासाद और इतने ही चीराहे थे । पूर्वोक्त जयवर्मदेव के 1258 ई. के लेख के अनुसार भोज के मेठ, जिक्रट आदि 104 प्रासाद थे -
नाम्ना यच्यतुरन्तारं शतमियन्मेरुत्रिवादयः ।
प्रसादा: जल……
इससे स्पष्ट है कि 104 की संख्या की पुष्टि साहित्य और शिलालेख दोनों से होती है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* According to Prabhachandra Dhara had 84 palaces and as many crossroads; per Jayavarmadeva's inscription of 1258 CE Bhoja had 104 prasadas such as Meru and Trikuta; so the number 104 is confirmed by both literature and inscription.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: According to Prabhachandra Dhara had 84 palaces and as many crossroads; per Jayavarmadeva's inscription of 1258 CE Bhoja had 104 prasadas such as Meru and Trikuta; so the number 104 is confirmed by both literature and inscription.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज स्वयं महान् निर्माता था । उल्लेखों से स्पष्ट है कि उसने शताधिक प्रासाद तो अपनी राजधानी धारा नगरी में ही वनवाये थे । धारा को उसने व्यवस्थित स्वासा ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Raja Bhoja was himself a great builder; references make clear he built over a hundred palaces in his capital Dhara alone; he planned Dhara in an orderly way.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Raja Bhoja was himself a great builder; references make clear he built over a hundred palaces in his capital Dhara alone; he planned Dhara in an orderly way.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
मालवा, मेवाङ़ में कितने ही मन्दिर बनवाये, पाठशालाएँ वनवार्थी। भारत की धार्मिक दृष्टि से एकसूत्र में वाँधने के लिए धारी सीमाओं पर केदार, रामेश्वर, सोमनाथ तथा मुण्डीर मन्दिर बनवाये और मध्य के उज्मैन में महाकाल का मन्दिर भी बनवाया। इस प्रक्रिया भोज वास्तुशारत्र और उसके निर्माण की वारीकियों का मर्मजा था। यह न केवल युक्तिकल्पता अविपतु समरांगणसूत्रधार से भी सिद्ध होता है।
*Gloss [my translation]:* He built many temples and schools in Malwa and Mewar; to bind India together religiously he built Kedara, Rameshvara, Somanatha and Mundira temples on the boundaries and the Mahakala temple at central Ujjain; in this he was a master of vastushastra and its construction subtleties, as both Yuktikalpataru and Samarangana-sutradhara show.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: He built many temples and schools in Malwa and Mewar; to bind India together religiously he built Kedara, Rameshvara, Somanatha and Mundira temples on the boundaries and the Mahakala temple at central Ujjain; in this he was a master of vastushastra and its construction subtleties, as both Yuktikalpataru and Samarangana-sutradhara show.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
चौसठ पद नामक पूरा नगर कल्पित करें । उसमें सोलह कोष्ठ, छः पथ और नौ चत्वर
(चौराहे) हो 14
चौकोर क्षेत्र में पूर्वे से पश्चिम आते चार भागों में तीन-तीन बॉस (वंश) का विभाजन
करें 15
छः बाँस के इस विभाजन में सोलह पद युक्त होने पर मध्यम वंश पर आश्रित शुभ
राजमार्ग बनाना चाहिए 16
*Gloss [my translation]:* Conceive the whole town as a sixty-four-pada grid, with sixteen kosthas, six paths and nine chatvaras (crossings); divide the square plot into four portions of three vamshas each; in this six-vamsha division of sixteen padas the auspicious royal road should be made on the middle vamsha.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Conceive the whole town as a sixty-four-pada grid, with sixteen kosthas, six paths and nine chatvaras (crossings); divide the square plot into four portions of three vamshas each; in this six-vamsha division of sixteen padas the auspicious royal road should be made on the middle vamsha.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
ज्येष्ठपुर चार हजार चाप (चार कोस या प्रायः बारह किलोमीटर क्षेत्रफल) का होता है। मध्य दो हजार का और एक हजार चाप (एक कोस) व्यास का अधम होता है 12
*Gloss [my translation]:* The best town is of four thousand capa (four kos, about twelve km); the middle of two thousand; the lowest is one thousand capa (one kos) in diameter.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: The best town is of four thousand capa (four kos, about twelve km); the middle of two thousand; the lowest is one thousand capa (one kos) in diameter.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
जो अशास्त्रज द्वारा और विना लक्षणों के ही किया गया तथा अनुपठान से पवित्र हुए विना ही किया गया वह अप्रशस्त और निष्णल होता है 173
ज्योतिधी और पुरोहित द्वारा शान्ति आदि अनुपठानों के बाद शास्त्रज शिल्पविद्ध स्थपति कर्म करे 174
पुरोहित अग्नि में हवन करे, ज्योतिपी स्थरता दे, स्थपति भेट पूजा करे - इस प्रकार शान्ति की योजना करे 175
जब नगर के मर्म (केन्द्र) में, चौराहे पर स्थायी रूप से स्थापित देवता निरन्तर पूर्ण जाते हैं तब उस नगर में शान्ति रहती है 176
*Gloss [my translation]:* Work done without shastra knowledge, without characteristics and without the rites is inauspicious and fruitless; after the astrologer and priest perform the propitiatory rites, the shastra-knowing sthapati should do the work; the priest offers oblation in fire, the astrologer gives stability, the sthapati makes offerings; when deities installed at the city's centre and crossroads are constantly worshipped, peace prevails in that city.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Work done without shastra knowledge, without characteristics and without the rites is inauspicious and fruitless; after the astrologer and priest perform the propitiatory rites, the shastra-knowing sthapati should do the work; the priest offers oblation in fire, the astrologer gives stability, the sthapati makes offerings; when deities installed at the city's centre and crossroads are constantly worshipped, peace prevails in that city.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
सुवर्णकार सहित सभी अग्निजीवी और अन्य मजदूरों को आग्नेय (पूर्व-दक्षिण) दिशा में वसाये 189
वैश्य-व्यापारी, जुआड़ी-धूतं, चक्रिक (तेली, कुक्शर, मुखविर) तथा नट-नर्तकों के घर दक्षिण में बनवाये 190
*Gloss [my translation]:* Settle all those who live by fire, including goldsmiths, and other labourers in the south-east; build in the south the houses of vaishya merchants, gamblers and rogues, oil-pressers and actors and dancers.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Settle all those who live by fire, including goldsmiths, and other labourers in the south-east; build in the south the houses of vaishya merchants, gamblers and rogues, oil-pressers and actors and dancers.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
विप्र पूर्व दिशाभाग में, क्षत्रिय पश्चिम में, वैश्य और शूद्र क्रमशः दक्षिण तथा उत्तर में किये जायें 1100
वणिक, वैद्य और मुख्य लोगों को घारों दिशाओं में वसायें । विशेषतः सेना को घारों दिशाओं में स्थापित करें ।101
नगर से वाहर पूर्व दिशा में लिंगस्थों (शैव या विभिन्न सम्प्रदायों) को वसायें । भशान और उसके निवासियों को ज्ञानी स्थपति दक्षिण में वसायें ।102
*Gloss [my translation]:* Brahmins in the east, kshatriyas in the west, vaishyas and shudras in the south and north respectively; merchants, physicians and chiefs in all four directions; the army especially on the four sides; outside the town in the east settle the lingasthas (Shaiva or sectarians); the wise sthapati should place the cremation ground and its inhabitants in the south.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern Hindi work, author and year unknown: attribute; corroborate before relying on it
gloss: Brahmins in the east, kshatriyas in the west, vaishyas and shudras in the south and north respectively; merchants, physicians and chiefs in all four directions; the army especially on the four sides; outside the town in the east settle the lingasthas (Shaiva or sectarians); the wise sthapati should place the cremation ground and its inhabitants in the south.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
यूअरवाले, भेड़ पालक, शिकारी, मछुआरे, दमनाधिकृत (दण्ड वाले अधिकारी) आहे नैन्ध्त्य दिशा में वसाये जाये 191
जो रथ और आयुध में कुशल हों वे सव नगर की परिश्रम दिशा में वसाये जाये 192
विभिन्न कर्मों के अधिकारी, सेवक, सुराजीवी कलाल आदि वायव्य दिशा में वसाये 193
यतियों के आश्रय, ब्रह्मवत्स (ब्राह्मण/ब्रह्मचारी) की सभा, प्रपा (प्याऊ) और पुण्यशाला (सदावर्त, मनिर्दर, धर्मशालादि) उत्तर में दिशा में वनवायें 194
घी तथा फल के विक्रता ईशान (पूर्वांत्तर) दिशा में वंसाये जाये तो उचित है 195

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
इन प्रस्थों में सर्वाधिक लोकप्रिय वल्लाल का भोजप्रवंध है । इसमें भोज, कालिदास और अन्य अनेक कवियों से सर्वन्धित छोटी-छोटी घटनाएँ हैं । वे सव मिलकर काव्यात्मक वातावरण वना देती हैं ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Among these works the most popular is Ballala's Bhojaprabandha, with short anecdotes about Bhoja, Kalidasa and many other poets, which together create a poetic atmosphere.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
शुभशील के भोजप्रबंध में कतिपय कथाएँ वल्लाल की पुस्तक जैसी भी हैं। रल्ननंदन गणि (1340 ई.) भोजप्रबंध में कतिपय कथाएँ वल्लाल की पुस्तक जैसी भी हैं । पद्मपुस्त ने भी किसी या रल्नमंदिर गणि (1460 ई.) के भोजप्रबंध में सात खंड हैं । पद्मपुस्त ने भी किसी भोजप्रबंध की रचना की थी । राजशेखर (सूरि?) का भी भोजप्रबंध रचा बताया जाता है । वत्सराजकृत भोजप्रबंध (वारहवीं सदी) का भी उल्लेख मिलता है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Shubhashila's Bhojaprabandha shares stories with Ballala's; Ratnanandana Gani (1340 CE) and Ratnamandira Gani (1460 CE) wrote Bhojaprabandhas (the latter in seven sections); Padmagupta, Rajashekhara (Suri?) and Vatsaraja (twelfth century) are also mentioned.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
इनके अतिरिक्त राजस्थानी, अवधी सहित विभिन्न भापाओं के काव्यग्रन्थों में भी भोज उपस्थित है। नरपति नाह् के बीसलदेव रासो, जायसी के पद्रायत, सिंढायय, दयालदास के पंवारवंशदर्पण, वाँकीदास री ख्यात, मालदेव के भोजचरित्र राहा और भोजचरित्र चौपाई, सारंग के भोजप्रवंध चतुप्पदी और भोजचरितरास, उदयभानु के भोजरासों, देवभद्र सूरि के श्रेयांसचरित, मुल्हण कवि के भोज राजा परकाया प्रदेशिनी पंद्रहवीं विशा कथा, हेमाणंद के भोज चरित्ररास, माघ का संवाद, कुशलधीर के भोजराजा चौपाई इत्यादि में इस राजा भोज के विषय में यथार्थ एवं कल्पित विभिन्न कथाएँ प्राप्त होती हैं।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja is present in verse works in various languages including Rajasthani and Avadhi; Jayasi's Padmavat, Dayaldas's Panwar-vansh-darpan, Bankidas's khyat, Maldev's Bhojacharitra and others contain both real and imagined tales of Raja Bhoja.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
इसीलिए कविजन अपने आय्यदाता की "नवभोज राज" अपथि से प्रशंसा करते थे। इस भोज के वंशज तेरहवीं सदी के अन्त में हुए अन्य राज भोज की प्रशंसा इस पूर्वज भोज की उपमा से की गयी - भोजो भोज इवापर:।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Hence poets praised their patron with the epithet 'New Bhojaraja'; a descendant of this Bhoja, another king Bhoja at the end of the thirteenth century, was praised by comparison with this ancestor: 'Bhoja is Bhoja's equal'.

book_title: The Udayeśvara Temple: Art, Architecture and Philosophy of the Śaiva Siddhānta — Anupa Pande
quote: Tattvaprakāśa, one of the most significant works on Śaiva Siddhānta, was authored by King Bhoja Paramāra of Malwa (1000-1055 CE). It expounds the three principles of the Lord (pati), the individual soul (paśu) and the fetters (pāśa) in accordance with the Śaivāgamas.

book_title: The Udayeśvara Temple: Art, Architecture and Philosophy of the Śaiva Siddhānta — Anupa Pande
quote:
Verse 75: The tattva of the tattvas has also been stated with ease by King Bhoja who has composed the Tattvaprakāśa.
Verse 76: That king, in whose mind the full reality (Śaivāgama) was disclosed in the manner of an āmalaka* placed on the palm,* he was king Śrī Bhojadeva, who for the sake of Śaivāgama composed the incomparable text called the Tattvaprakāśa.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: From the literary and epigraphic sources contemporary with the Paramaras, it is learnt that the founding ancestor of this line was born from the sacrificial fire-pit (अग्निकुण्ड) of the sage Vasishtha (वसिष्ठ). No sooner was he born than he drove away the foe (*par*, i.e. enemies) by slaying them; hence the true name of that hero became "Paramar" (परमार).

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: The names of various kings of the Paramara dynasty, such as Upendra (उपेन्द्र), are found. Among them, Siyak (सीयक) or Shriharsha (श्रीहर्ष) is the first Paramara king whose tenth-century copper-plate grants are found. He had two sons: Vakpatiraja Munj (वाक्पतिराज मुंज) and Sindhuraja (सिन्धुराज) or Sindhul (सिन्धुल).

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: The event of King Bhoj's ancestors obtaining the kingdom of Malwa is described in the *Prabandha-chintamani*. According to it, the ancestors of Mularaja ruled at Kalyanakataka in Kanyakubja. Then Bhumada or Bhumadeva became ruler. That famous king donated the whole of Malwa to Mahakaleshvara, the lord of Ujjayini, and appointed the Paramara family as its foster-protector.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: According to this story it is clearly evident that the Paramaras were once the protection-officers of Mahakal's Malava region, who later, getting the opportunity, became its masters. Full sovereignty over the kingdom was attained by King Munj, and it was conferred with the supreme glory by Maharaja Bhojadeva.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern popular account (Rajpurohit): attribute; never adopt its claims as settled

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: For reasons of security, King Bhoj shifted his capital from Ujjain to Dhar. Before this, he had duly settled and developed the city of Dhara to befit a capital, making it attractive with a rampart (प्राकार / outer fortification wall), a moat (परिखा / outer ditch), and — in the manner of the age — up-to-date gardens, lakes and the like. Then, following that same plan, he also re-founded Ujjain, Vidisha (विदिशा) and others afresh. Near Bhopal and near Patna he founded new cities named Bhojpur (भोजपुर) after himself.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern popular account (Rajpurohit): attribute; never adopt its claims as settled

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: Many copper-plate grants and stone inscriptions of King Bhoj are found. References to King Bhoj occur also in the inscriptions of other contemporary kings. Abundant references to Bhoj are found also in the poetry, treatises and so forth of the Bhoj period. In later inscriptions, texts, traditions, folk-tales, proverbs and poems, countless references to and accounts of King Bhoj are found. Our knowledge of King Bhoj from history proper is limited, but from traditional literature, oral traditions and the like we obtain much more. Thus, in gaining knowledge of King Bhoj's personality and achievements, history and tradition become mutually complementary.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern popular account (Rajpurohit): attribute; never adopt its claims as settled

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: A text of 1055 CE was written during King Bhoj's reign; from this it is clear that King Bhoj was alive up to 1055. According to the *Ain-i-Akbari* (आइने-अकबरी), King Bhoj's age was 90 years. From various texts it is learnt that King Bhoj ruled over an India extending from Gauda/Bengal (गौड़) to the Deccan (दक्षिणापथ) for 55 years, 7 months and 3 days. Subtracting 90 from 1055 gives about 965 as the apparent time of King Bhoj's birth. If King Bhoj ruled up to 1055, then subtracting 55 years, 7 months and 3 days from that makes his accession possible around 999 CE.
tier_note: T9 heritage or popular narrative: modern popular account (Rajpurohit): attribute; never adopt its claims as settled

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: Thus, by defeating various known and unknown kings — Gangeyadeva the Kalachuri king of Chedi, Tailapa II the Chalukya king of Karnataka, Indraratha the king of Adinagara, Bhimadeva of Lata, Rajyapala the Gurjara-Pratihara king of Kanyakubja, the Turushka (Turk) king, Viryarama the Chauhan king of Shakambhari, Abhimanyu the king of Dubkund, Bhillama (III) the king of Vidarbha and Marathwada, and others — Bhoj made his power and the extent of his realm all-India in reach. Hundreds of kings and great kings honoured Bhoj as their "Maharajadhiraja Parameshvara" (supreme sovereign of sovereigns) and constantly strove, through offerings of daughters in marriage (kanyopayana) and the like, to keep King Bhoj ever pleased.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: Of all of them, Munj — because Bhojdev was the most capable — made Bhoj alone king. At this the other brothers and kinsmen of the family became displeased. But in the end the kingdom remained in King Bhoj's hands, and he securely enjoyed the pleasures of sovereignty all his life.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: But in the *Navasahasanka-charita* and in Bhoj's copper-plates, Sindhul too is called king — probably because, after Munj's sudden death, it was Sindhuraja who for some years conducted the governance like a regent on Bhoj's behalf, since Bhoj must have remained absorbed in his pursuit of learning. This is why neither any copper-plate nor any inscription of Sindhuraja is found. Yet even then he enjoyed kingship; and so Bhoj and the later kings too, out of respect, called Sindhuraja a king. But when Sindhuraja died in a battle, King Bhoj himself had to take up the reins of governance. This was around 999 CE.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: King Bhoj not only composed a voluminous treatise on craft such as the *Samarangana-sutradhara*, but also founded the cities of Dharanagari, Ujjayini, Vidisha (Bhaillasvamipur / भाइल्लस्वामीपुर), Bhojpur (Raisen / रायसेन) and the Bhojpur near Patna. He shifted his capital from Ujjayini to Dharanagari, which was his hereditary capital, because it was a secure place. He shifted Ujjain from the Gadhkalika (गढ़कालिका) area and re-founded it toward Mahakal. He re-founded Vidisha under the name Bhaillasvamipur, which was later called Bhelsa (भेलसा).

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: In Sindhuraja's time, Dhara was the hereditary capital of the Paramaras and Ujjayini the chief capital. Naturally, at the time of Bhoj's accession too, Ujjain was the capital. But for the security of his own rule from enemies and from his own kinsmen, he conferred upon his hereditary capital itself the glory of the chief capital. Bhoj bestowed upon Dhara the glory of Ujjain.

quote: King Bhoj of Malwa, in the first half of the eleventh century, composed many works on various subjects. Some of those books relate to royal living and administration. He was himself a capable king; hence the authenticity, in this regard, of the books written by him or in his time cannot be doubted. In his vast work named the *Samarangana-sutradhara*, the various forms and shapes of royal palaces are discussed in detail.

quote: King Bhoj's *Yukti-kalpataru* is a work on various subjects for the knowledge of princes. In it are briefly described those subjects that were expected, in that age, of kings and princes. This book has nearly two thousand verses.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: According to the works found relating to King Bhoj, he was a peerless patron of poets and artists. Five hundred scholars, poets and artists enjoyed his patronage. Among them, many authors are famous — including Dhanapala, Halayudha, Chhittapa, Amitagati, Ubbata and Purantaka. The image of Vagdevi, made by the capable sculptor Manathala patronized by him, was made in Samvat 1091 (1034 CE), which is today in the museum in London.

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: This Gangeyadeva had humiliated and killed King Munj. According to the *Prabandha-chintamani*, when King Bhoj became king, a play of this killing was shown to him. Angered, King Bhoj attacked him and won a glorious victory over him. In the *Parijata-manjari* play — composed in the eulogy of King Bhoj's descendant Arjunavarman (1210 to 1218) — at its beginning (1/3) it is stated that, on his wish being fulfilled, King Bhojadeva held a "Gangeyadeva-bhangotsava" (festival of Gangeyadeva's rout).

book_title: King Bhoj and Paramara-period Town Architecture (Raja Bhoj aur Parmarkaleen Nagar Sthapatya) — English translation — Bhagwatilal Rajpurohit
quote: But King Bhoj conquered even him, and on the occasion of the festival of the conquest of that Gangeyadeva Telang, Bhoj erected this iron pillar, which was later, in the Muslim period, broken in an attempt to remove it from its place and take it to Ahmedabad; and the removers, it being broken, left it there. Those weight-stones were for firming the pillar in the ground; and on that platform, amid those stones, the whole 44-foot-high iron pillar had been erected. book_title: The Hindu Temple, Volume I — Stella Kramrisch
quote: In the ‘Samarāṅganasūtradhāra’, a treatise on architecture, the author, King Bhoja of Dhārā, who ruled over Mālava in the first part of the eleventh century, says: “He, who begins to work as an architect (sthapati) without knowing the science of architecture (vāstuśāstra) and proud with false knowledge must be put to death by the king as one who ruins the kingdom (rājahiṃsaka); dead before his time, his ghost will wander on this wide earth. He, who though well versed in the traditional science is not skilled in the work will faint at the time of action like a timid man on the battle-field. He, who is expert only in his workmanship, but unable to understand the meaning of the traditional science, will like a blind man be misled by anyone’ (S.S. XLIV. 6-10).
